data.title: Carlsberg plans an IPO for its India unit
data.description:
Carlsberg India, the country's second-largest brewer, plans to sell up to 86.4M shares, or about 15% of the company, through an entirely secondary offering. That will mean an infusion of cash for Danish parent Carlsberg (CABGY). The latest reports say the IPO could raise as much as $600M at a $4B valuation. The IPO could launch as early as December.   

The Securities and Exchange Board of India approved the IPO, which had been filed under its confidential pre-filing route. Carlsberg India reported revenue of 87.09B rupees for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. The company runs seven breweries and holds a 21.9% market share across 16 key states and union territories in India.

Looking ahead, Carlsberg (CABGY) shareholders will still benefit from the unit's growth, and the results in India will be public and closely watched by the market.

data.title: Weight Watchers uses $10M cash to retire $16.3M in loan debt
data.description:
• WW International (WW) announced on Friday that it used $10M in cash to retire approximately $16.3M of outstanding term loan debt through a discounted prepayment offer.

  • The company said the debt reduction, combined with earlier repayments, has lowered its total debt by 12.4% this year.

data.title: Columbia Financial CFO Thomas Splaine to step down
data.description:
Columbia Financial (CLBK) on Friday said Thomas Splaine is set to step down from the role of executive vice president and CFO, effective December 18.

Splaine decided to resign for personal reasons.

Shares were 1.38% lower at $10.74 during pre-market trading.

Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Banking Officer Dennis Gibney has been appointed to the additional post of interim CFO.

data.title: Trump to meet Abdul El-Sayed on golden ‘TrumpCare’ proposal
data.description:
President Donald Trump has indicated his willingness to meet with Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed to discuss the Michigan Democrat’s push to expand Medicare for all Americans, an initiative the latter agreed to rebrand as “TrumpCare.”

“I know I’ll be meeting with him,” Trump said during an interview with The New York Post on Tuesday. “Maybe there’s some place in the middle that we could go," he added without specifying the date for the meeting.

Despite Democratic control in Congress, Trump will have to sign, not veto, any proposed legislation on 'Medicare for All,' largely a leftist push to replace private insurance with a publicly funded single-payer national health program.

Championed by progressive Dems such as El-Sayed, 'Medicare for All' represents an area Republicans have long opposed given its potential to increase government spending. Universal healthcare could increase federal subsidies for health care from $1.5T to $3T by 2030, the Congressional Budget Office estimated in 2022.

El-Sayed reiterated his push for “Medicare for All” earlier this month, even agreeing to call it  “Trumpcare.”

"Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave," he wrote in a social media post with mock images of golden TrumpCare cards attached to get Trump’s attention.

When asked about the golden “TrumpCare” plan, the president called El-Sayed “a smart guy.” “I’m just going to veto everything there is,” he said, adding that healthcare is one area he is willing to negotiate with Democrats on.

“Then at some point I think they’re going to want to negotiate. I will, and we can do health care. We can do a lot of great things together,” Trump said.

Dear readers, we recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: OceanaGold secures Ausgold shareholder approval for acquisition
data.description:
• OceanaGold (OGC:CA) said on Friday Ausgold shareholders approved its proposed acquisition of 100% of Ausgold's issued shares through a scheme of arrangement, with 99.4% of votes cast in favour.

  • Under the deal, Ausgold shareholders will receive 0.03365 OceanaGold shares for each Ausgold share held or could elect to receive A$1.36 per share in cash, subject to scale-back.

  • The transaction includes a maximum cash pool of A$194M ($129M).

  • The acquisition is expected to take effect on December 2, 2026, pending court approval, with completion scheduled for December 11.

  • Ausgold shareholders are expected to own 6%-8% of OceanaGold following completion. 

  • Share +2.65%

data.title: Coca-Cola continues its refranchising strategy with a deal in Africa
data.description:
Coca-Cola Company (KO) and Gutsche Family Investments have completed the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Pty. Ltd. to Coca-Cola HBC AG (CCHBF) after receiving all necessary regulatory approvals in Africa.

Coca-Cola Beverages Africa is a Johannesburg-based company and the largest Coca-Cola (KO) bottler in Africa. It operates in 14 countries and handles about 40% of all Coca-Cola (KO) volume sold on the continent. It was formed by merging the Southern and East African bottling businesses of The Coca-Cola Company (KO), SABMiller, and Gutsche Family Investments and began operating as its own company in July 2016. In October 2025, Coca-Cola (KO) and Gutsche Family Investments agreed to sell a 75% stake to Swiss-based Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF) for about $2.6B, valuing CCBA at $3.4B.

Of note, Coca-Cola (KO) and Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF) have a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa held by Coca-Cola (KO) within a six-year period.

The completion of the transaction was noted to mark another significant milestone in Coca-Cola's ongoing strategy to refranchise company-owned and controlled bottling operations. "This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations," stated Coca-Cola (KO) CEO Henrique Braun. "CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC  brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise, and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth," he added.

data.title: Railtown AI targets lower AI costs with new model testing tools
data.description:
• Railtown AI Technologies (RLAIF) announced on Friday new AI model evaluation tools that let developers compare AI models using data from actual application runs.
  • The tools will help developers find lower-cost alternatives, including Apple (AAPL)'s on-device AI models and privately hosted models, without compromising performance or data privacy.
  • The technology could help reduce AI costs and reliance on external providers.
  • Enterprises and governments can use the technology to assess models running on infrastructure they control, particularly for sensitive data.
  • Railtown expects to make the evaluation tools available soon and plans to publish a technical blog demonstrating their use.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Anthropic stock gains premarket, reclaiming IPO price
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) shares rose 3.3% in premarket trading Friday, looking to recover some ground after a rocky start to life as a publicly traded company.

The stock snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, ending 1.08% higher ahead of the Thanksgiving break.

The three straight sessions of losses in its first five trading sessions pushed the stock to $82.79, below its $83 IPO price. The decline has wiped out the gains from its much-anticipated Nasdaq debut.

In its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50 and hit an intraday high of $115.10.

Anthropic has struggled to join the broader AI rally that briefly lifted technology stocks following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's dramatic return to the company. While the rally boosted sentiment across the AI trade, Anthropic shares largely missed out.

Investors have raised concerns about Anthropic's $900B spending commitments, while bond investors expect its debt to receive a junk rating.

data.title: Search Minerals announces C$1.4M secured convertible loan
data.description:
• Search Minerals (SHCMF) said  on Friday it entered into a binding term sheet with lenders, including major shareholders Petra Holdings and Harder Investments, for a C$1.4M secured convertible loan carrying 8.5% annual interest and a conversion price of C$0.30 per share.

  • The company plans to use most of the proceeds to repay a C$700K overdue convertible note owed to Texas Critical Minerals.

  • The refinancing is expected to lower interest costs on the TCM debt to 8.5% from 15% and extend debt maturities.
  • Repayment of the overdue TCM debt is expected to reduce the company's working capital deficit, subject to final accounting treatment, while providing additional funds for general working capital.
  • The transaction is expected to resolve one of three claims filed by TCM. The company continues to dispute the two remaining claims.
  • Closing is targeted for mid-December 2026.
  • The transaction constitutes a related-party deal, as both Petra Holdings and Harder Investments own more than 10% of Search Minerals' voting securities.
  •  Petra is also controlled by company director Michael Pearson.
  • Share -9.87%
